title: River of Water of Life, Rev 22:1
text_faithful: Revelation 22:1 describes 'a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.' The faith view records this image exactly: a river, pure, clear, and flowing from the throne, at the centre of the city.
engineering: The engineering view treats the river as a water-system brief: a clear, continuously flowing urban watercourse requires a source, a channel, a flow rate, water-quality management, and a destination. Clarity in engineering means low turbidity and controlled biology, achieved by treatment and flow, not by declaration.
body:
History and description: Urban rivers historically served drinking, transport, power, and waste removal at once, which is why they were both vital and polluted. A river designed for clarity must separate those functions, so that drinking-quality water is not also the waste channel.

Science proof: Science proof, as water-quality method: clarity is measured by turbidity in nephelometric turbidity units (NTU), with drinking water commonly below 1 NTU. The demo converts a sample's clarity description into a turbidity band and verdict.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: the demo reports turbidity values for three samples and the drinking-water verdict against a 1 NTU threshold.

title: Tree of Life: Twelve Fruits
text_faithful: Revelation 22:2 describes the tree of life bearing twelve manner of fruits, yielding her fruit every month. The faith view records the twelvefold fruiting exactly; it does not name twelve species, and this record does not invent species for the text.
engineering: The engineering and botanical reading asks what twelve fruits could mean in a real orchard: twelve fruiting types, twelve harvest months, or twelve varieties in rotation. Each reading is a different orchard design, and the record keeps them as alternatives rather than choosing one silently.

A twelve-month harvest therefore requires either multiple species, multiple climates, controlled environments, or stored fruit, and a real design must say which.

Science proof: Science proof, as orchard arithmetic: the demo builds a twelve-month harvest table from four species with staggered seasons, showing which months are covered by fresh fruit and which require storage, the honest version of a twelve-fruit claim.

title: Monthly Fruiting Cycles, Real Botany Versus Text
text_faithful: The faith view states monthly fruiting (Revelation 22:2). Real botany states that fruiting is seasonal, governed by chilling hours, daylight, temperature, and species, and this record puts the two side by side without merging them.
engineering: Deciduous fruit trees need winter chilling to break dormancy; tropical fruits need heat and rainfall patterns; citrus fruits in warm climates can hold fruit across months but still fruit in seasons. No temperate tree produces a new ripe crop every month of the year outdoors.
body:
History and description: Controlled-environment agriculture changes the picture partially: greenhouses with heating, lighting, and irrigation can extend seasons and stagger crops, but at energy and water cost, and still per crop, not per tree. The text's monthly tree and the greenhouse's monthly harvest are different achievements.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo computes chilling-hour accumulation for a model winter (hours below 7 degrees Celsius) and compares it with a 400-hour requirement, standard orchard arithmetic.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: chilling hours accumulate only in cold hours; the demo totals a twelve-week model and reports whether the requirement is met.

title: River Ecology: Clear Water Systems
text_faithful: The faith view describes a pure river (Revelation 22:1); river ecology describes what actually lives in clear water and what keeps it clear, which is a biological balance, not a static property.
engineering: Clear water supports rooted plants, invertebrates, and fish that need oxygen and low sediment, while nutrient overload (nitrogen and phosphorus) grows algae, clouds water, and depletes oxygen when the algae decay. Clarity is therefore an outcome of nutrient control, flow, shading, and biology together.
body:
History and description: Urban clear-water systems use constructed wetlands, gravel beds, and planted margins to filter nutrients and sediment before water reaches the main channel, mimicking natural floodplain filtration at engineered scale.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo applies a simplified nutrient-balance model, showing downstream nutrient concentration falling as wetland area increases, the core constructed-wetland result.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: downstream concentration equals inflow times exp(-rate times area), a first-order removal model.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

Status label: established. Faith and engineering views are kept distinct in this record; nothing speculative is presented as established, and nothing established is presented as speculative.

engineering: A supply system is sized by demand: population times per-person use, plus commercial, irrigation, and fire flows, plus losses. Storage covers peak hours and outages; pressure must stay high enough to reach upper floors and low enough not to burst pipes.

title: Water Recycling and Treatment
text_faithful: The faith view describes pure water; recycling and treatment are the engineering means by which used water becomes pure again, through physical, biological, and chemical steps in sequence.
engineering: Treatment stages are: screening and settling (solids), biological treatment (microbes consuming dissolved waste), filtration (fine particles), and disinfection (ultraviolet light or chlorine). No single stage does the whole job, and the sequence is the system.
body:
History and description: Recycled water for irrigation and non-drinking uses is established practice worldwide; recycled water for drinking (potable reuse) requires additional treatment and monitoring, and is adopted only with regulatory approval and continuous testing.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo applies removal efficiencies per stage multiplicatively, showing how four stages at 90, 90, 99, and 99.9 percent removal combine to a very low remaining fraction.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: remaining fraction equals the product of (1 - efficiency) across stages.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

title: River Hydrology Model
text_faithful: The faith view describes a river flowing from the throne through the city (Revelation 22:1); hydrology models how fast a river flows, given its channel shape, slope, and roughness, using the Manning equation, an established empirical formula.
engineering: The Manning equation states that velocity equals (1/n) times hydraulic radius to the two-thirds power times slope to the one-half power, where n is a roughness coefficient (about 0.03 for a clean natural channel, higher for weedy or rocky channels). Discharge equals velocity times cross-sectional area.
body:
History and description: The model is empirical, not exact: it predicts well for steady, uniform flow and poorly for floods, bends, and obstructions, which is why real river design pairs it with physical measurement and safety margins.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo computes velocity and discharge for a model channel 10 metres wide, 1 metre deep, slope 0.001, roughness 0.03, standard Manning arithmetic.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: hydraulic radius equals area divided by wetted perimeter; velocity follows Manning; discharge equals velocity times area.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

Status label: established. Faith and engineering views are kept distinct in this record; nothing speculative is presented as established, and nothing established is presented as speculative.

Sources: Sources: standard open-channel hydraulics (Manning equation). Signature edition: this record is an original Signature presentation of the same subject, with its own id prefix and edition slug.
demo:
import math
width, depth, slope, n = 10.0, 1.0, 0.001, 0.03
area = width * depth
perimeter = width + 2 * depth
R = area / perimeter
v = (1 / n) * R ** (2 / 3) * math.sqrt(slope)
print(f'hydraulic radius: {R:.3f} m')
print(f'velocity: {v:.2f} m/s')
print(f'discharge: {v * area:.2f} m3/s')
expected_output:
hydraulic radius: 0.833 m
velocity: 0.93 m/s
discharge: 9.33 m3/s

body:

title: Irrigation and Water Demand
text_faithful: The faith view describes a river watering the city's trees (Revelation 22:1-2); irrigation engineering computes how much of that water trees actually need, given climate, species, and soil, using reference evapotranspiration.
engineering: Crop water need equals reference evapotranspiration (ETo) times a crop coefficient (Kc), times area, divided by irrigation efficiency. ETo in a hot, dry Levantine summer can reach 6 to 8 mm per day, while winter ETo may be 1 to 2 mm per day, so demand varies several-fold across the year.
body:
History and description: Drip irrigation, delivering water directly to roots, reaches efficiencies of 85 to 95 percent, versus 60 to 75 percent for sprinklers and lower for flood irrigation, which is why drip dominates modern orchards in water-scarce regions.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo computes daily irrigation demand for a one-hectare orchard at summer ETo 7 mm, Kc 0.8, and 90 percent efficiency, standard irrigation arithmetic.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: demand equals ETo times Kc times area divided by efficiency, converted from millimetres to cubic metres (1 mm over 1 hectare equals 10 cubic metres).

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

title: River Water Quality Measures
text_faithful: The faith view describes pure water (Revelation 22:1); water-quality measurement defines purity operationally, through parameters with thresholds, instruments, and sampling schedules, not through appearance alone.
engineering: Standard river-quality parameters are: turbidity (clarity), dissolved oxygen (life support, commonly above 6 mg/L for healthy rivers), pH (commonly 6.5 to 8.5), nitrate and phosphate (nutrients), biochemical oxygen demand (organic pollution), and faecal indicator bacteria (health risk). Clear-looking water can fail bacterial tests, and cloudy water can pass chemical tests, which is why all parameters are measured.
body:
History and description: Monitoring is scheduled, not occasional: continuous sensors for temperature, oxygen, and turbidity, plus laboratory samples for nutrients and bacteria, with results compared against thresholds and trends tracked over seasons.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo evaluates a sample against five thresholds and reports a pass count and overall verdict, the standard compliance calculation.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: each parameter passes if within its threshold band; overall verdict requires all five passes.

title: Flood and Drainage Safety
text_faithful: The faith view describes a river in the city; flood safety describes what happens when that river rises, and it is a life-safety requirement, not an optional extra, for any river-adjacent planting or building.
engineering: Flood design uses a design storm: rainfall intensity for a chosen return period (for example, a 100-year storm) over the catchment, converted to peak flow by the rational method (flow equals runoff coefficient times intensity times area), then compared with channel capacity.
body:
History and description: Safety measures are: channel capacity above design flow, flood walls or levees where needed, drainage that keeps streets passable, warning systems, and evacuation routes that do not cross the flood path. A garden court below flood level without drainage is a drowning and damage risk, stated plainly.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo applies the rational method to a model catchment and compares peak flow with channel capacity, reporting the margin.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: peak flow Q equals C times i times A, with unit conversion; the demo uses C 0.6, intensity 50 mm per hour, area 2 square kilometres.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

Status label: established. Faith and engineering views are kept distinct in this record; nothing speculative is presented as established, and nothing established is presented as speculative.

Sources: Sources: standard flood-design practice (rational method, simplified, stated here). Signature edition: this record is an original Signature presentation of the same subject, with its own id prefix and edition slug.

print(f'channel capacity (assumption): 25.0 m3/s')
print(f"margin: {25.0 - Q:.1f} m3/s, adequate = {Q <= 25.0}")

title: River-and-Tree System Integration
text_faithful: The faith view joins river and tree in one image (Revelation 22:1-2): water flowing, trees fruiting, leaves present, all in the same place. The integration record joins them as a system: water supply feeds irrigation, irrigation feeds trees, trees shade the river, shade cools the water, and cool water supports river ecology.
engineering: Integration is where systems help or harm each other: shade reduces evaporation but drops leaves that raise nutrient load; irrigation draws down river flow but returns drainage; flood protection for trees changes the river channel. A system design must list these interactions and decide each one, rather than designing water and trees separately and hoping they agree.
body:
History and description: The integration test is a balance sheet: water in (river, rain, recycling) must equal water out (drinking, irrigation, evaporation, outflow) within storage limits, and nutrient in must equal nutrient out within ecological limits, over a full year, not a single day.

Science proof: Science proof, as systems arithmetic: the demo builds a simplified annual water balance for a model district and checks that inflow, outflow, and storage change balance, the fundamental integration audit.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: inflow minus outflow equals storage change; the demo reports all three and the balance verdict.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

Status label: integrated. Faith and engineering views are kept distinct in this record; nothing speculative is presented as established, and nothing established is presented as speculative.

Sources: Sources: standard water-balance practice; Revelation 22:1-2 for the integrated image; this system design is a Signature-generated completion for this suite, with provenance stated here. Signature edition: this record is an original Signature presentation of the same subject, with its own id prefix and edition slug.
demo:
inflow = 1200000
outflow = 1150000
storage_change = inflow - outflow
print(f'annual inflow: {inflow:,} m3')
print(f'annual outflow: {outflow:,} m3')
print(f'storage change: {storage_change:,} m3')
print(f'balanced: {inflow == outflow + storage_change}')
expected_output:
annual inflow: 1,200,000 m3
annual outflow: 1,150,000 m3
storage change: 50,000 m3
balanced: True
